- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period (e.g., sentiment <0.3), model often overshoots; cap upward revisions at +3% of recent 7-day average.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment oscillates 0.3–0.7), model frequently underestimates downward moves; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to downward forecasts.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 day horizons.
- For 30-day forecasts, if recent 10-day average price > forecast, model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with trend.
- If sentiment is high and forecast is below true outcome, model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–7 days to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
